title: Directional Flow and Mirrored Corner Panels
description: Introduce an explicit directional-flow system for the UI library (ui/js/react/index.tsx): every element gets a horizontal flow (ltr|rtl) and vertical flow (down|up), default LTR+down with icons at the trailing edge (label-then-icon, flipping today's icon-first order globally for Button/Toggle/Action/tab buttons). Tree rows keep icon at flow-start. Mechanism: a FlowProvider React context (cloned from the LevelProvider pattern) that CornerPanel sets from its corner via flowFromCorner(); horizontal mirroring rides on native CSS `dir="rtl"` on the corner-panel root so flex/grid auto-mirror (Tailwind v4's divide-x already emits logical border-inline-*, and built-in logical utilities like text-start/ms-auto exist). Right corners (top-right, bottom-right) become full horizontal mirrors: icon left of label, right-aligned text, tree gutter/chevron/guides on the right, scrollbar on the left. Bottom corners keep only their existing chrome+tab-row vertical mirror (tree content stays top-to-bottom). Work includes: ui.css logical utility additions (ms-*/me-*/ps-*/pe-* alongside existing ml-*/mr-*/pl-*/pr-*), FlowProvider/useFlow/flowFromCorner region, icon-trailing flips at ButtonGroupItem/ToggleGroupItem/ActionGroupItem/Action/PanelTabRow, dir wiring on CornerPanel + portalled overlay content (Popover/Select/Tooltip/Dialog/ContextMenu), physical-to-logical class conversions at enumerated flow-relative sites (tree gutter/guides, labels, navbar toggle, command shortcut, kbd, dropdown check icon, detail-panel, toggle-strip separator) while windows/mode-dock/canvas stay physical, dock drag-and-drop insert-index math inversion for RTL rows in computeTabDockDropZone, test updates/additions, and periphery (ui-interpreter.tsx value row, Storybook Panel stories). Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-the-design-language-quirky-sifakis.md.
summary:
Added a `direction` axis to the Tree component so its foldable groups unfold in the direction the hosting panel actually grows (matching the existing Ribbon `"up"`/`"down"` pattern), and wired corner panels to it — bottom-corner panels' trees now unfold upward instead of always downward.

Design (per explicit owner decisions this round): `direction` is a public, explicit prop on `Tree` (`"down"` default | `"up"`), not solely an ambient behavior — any consumer can opt in. Within one expanded group, children fully reverse order (last child ends up nearest its own header), not just relocate as a block — mirroring how Ribbon stacks nested tab-bar rows. The fold chevron flips both its collapsed and expanded glyph for `"up"`: `chevron-left`/`chevron-up` instead of `chevron-right`/`chevron-down` — a deliberate pairing that echoes this feature set's existing mirrored/reversed (`left`+`up`) vs default (`right`+`down`) vocabulary.

Implementation (`ui/js/react/index.tsx`):
- New `TreeDirection` type + `treeFoldChevronIcon(direction, open)` helper; `direction?: TreeDirection` added to `TreeContext` (optional — forwarded explicitly at every recursive `level+1` provider reconstruction so it survives nesting; the ~20 leaf/test-only context providers elsewhere are untouched and implicitly stay `"down"`, which is correct/unchanged for them).
- `Tree`'s own `direction` prop (default `"down"`) reverses its top-level `sections` array and feeds `direction` into its root `TreeContext.Provider`.
- `TreeDataSectionView`/`TreeDataItemView` (the data-driven `sections`-prop rendering path) read `direction` from context and reverse their own `items`/`childItems` arrays before mapping — recomputing `isLastItem`/`isLastSection` against the already-reversed array so guide-line continuation stays consistent with actual render order.
- `TreeSection` and `TreeItem`'s two group-row variants (`"property"` and default layout) now build their header and branch-content as two named JSX values and render them in swapped order when `direction==="up"` (content before header) — for `TreeSection` this meant swapping which of Radix's `CollapsibleTrigger`/`CollapsibleContent` renders first (DOM order, not Radix subcomponent identity, controls layout — Radix's `Collapsible.Root` doesn't require a fixed child order); for `TreeItem`'s plain conditional-render variants it's a direct JSX reorder.
- `PanelTreeUnitsPane` (the tree host inside `CornerPanel`) now reads `useFlow().block` and passes it as `<Tree direction={flow.block} />` — since the panel's content wrapper only forces `inline="ltr"` (from the earlier tree-mirroring-exemption fix) while still inheriting `block` from the corner's own flow, this correctly yields `"up"` for bottom corners and `"down"` for top corners with no new wiring needed beyond this one prop.

Explicitly out of scope this round (documented, not silently dropped): `SortableTreeItem` (a separate dnd-kit-based tree variant, currently unused anywhere in the app — verified via repo-wide grep) and the unrelated `control-tree-folder`/`window-measure-tree` (asset/file picker, mode-dock window options) group renderers were left at their existing hardcoded "down" behavior — none are reachable from a corner panel today, so this doesn't affect the actual feature surface; a future consumer of any of these could still get "up" support by threading `direction` through the same way. Guide-line vertical connector visuals (the elbow/stem lines) are not direction-aware — in "up" mode they may still visually anchor as if extending downward; this is an accepted, documented visual approximation rather than a functional issue, out of scope for this pass' effort budget.

Tests added (4, all passing): sibling-order reversal + content-before-header DOM order for a data-driven `Tree` with `direction="up"`; chevron pair for `direction="up"` open/closed vs `direction="down"`; end-to-end `CornerPanel` integration test confirming `corner="bottom-left"` yields reversed section order in its rendered content while `corner="top-left"` keeps declared order.

Verified: full `ui-react` vitest suite passes with the same stable 14 pre-existing/unrelated failures as every prior check this session (same concurrent-dev-driven Tree/Layout/Shell churn traced earlier — none newly introduced).
